item.title: Vancouver mayor’s apologies won’t fix Orr misinformation controversy, says expert
item.description: Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim is still facing backlash after he apologized for a third time Wednesday over his false accusations about COPE Coun. Sean Orr.

item.title: Canada’s defence chief says allies may help Gulf states bombed by Iran
item.description: Canada’s defence chief Gen. Jennie Carignan says allies are in talks about possibly helping Persian Gulf states defend themselves against bombing from Iran. Carignan says a meeting is set for Friday to discuss such a proposal among allied militaries and the Canadian Armed Forces would present a recommendation to the government. She did not specify […]

item.title: Eby says OpenAI’s Altman will apologize to Tumbler Ridge in wake of shootings
item.description: B.C.'s premier says OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has agreed to apologize to the people of Tumbler Ridge after the mass shooting by a user of the firm's technology.

item.title: Police used neck restraint on B.C. man who died after altercation: paramedic
item.description: A paramedic testifying at a public hearing into the 2015 death of Myles Gray says he had trouble intubating the man.

item.title: Poilievre says he has reservations about Carney’s suggested fiscal watchdog
item.description: OTTAWA — Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre says he has “serious” reservations about Prime Minister Mark Carney’s suggestion for a new Parliamentary Budget Officer and is calling for the latest interim watchdog to get the job. item.title: Kerry Sim, who killed B.C. teen Reena Virk in 1997, loses parole revocation appeal
item.description: The killer of British Columbia teenager Reena Virk has lost an appeal over the cancellation of her day parole last year following a positive drug test result.

item.title: Expert warns of incorrect flagging amid OpenAI standard review
item.description: As OpenAI moves to strengthen its policies and reporting system, a professor at UBC believes more users will be wrongfully flagged.

item.title: Coroner says B.C. teen was forced into water by dingoes in Australia
item.description: A coroner in Australia has determined that a 19-year-old B.C. woman drowned when she was attacked by a pack of dingoes on an early morning walk.

item.title: Langley RCMP officer injured after police cruiser rollover
item.description: A Langley RCMP officer is injured after a single-vehicle collision that resulted in a police cruiser being flipped over, Mounties say.

item.title: Partner sentenced for indignity to human remains in death of Maple Ridge woman
item.description: The man who was found guilty of indignity to human remains in connection with the death of a Maple Ridge woman was sentenced Thursday.
